submission.natural_language_explanation: An induction (copy) head: at a token that already appeared earlier in the same text it attends to the token that followed the earlier occurrence (mostly the nearest one) and reproduces that position's representation in the residual stream, so it peaks one token before the token that continued the earlier copy. It stays near its resting write at first occurrences, in prose with no verbatim repeat, and at single duplicated words, and crosses the active line where a verbatim chunk of about four or more tokens (in practice a repeated clause or sentence, a recurring code or markup line, a repeated name or number) is being continued.

rival_explanations: A plain duplicate-token copy head: it fires whenever the current token occurred earlier, however short the surrounding match, and copies that earlier token itself, so a lone repeated word (' the red ball ... the blue ball') or a two-token echo activates it as much as a repeated sentence.

A long-repeat head that needs a whole sentence or several copies of a chunk: clause-length repeats of eight to twelve tokens and simple repeated sentences stay below the active line, so its write only becomes large for paragraph-scale verbatim repetition.
